A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ProbeGen research and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. v1 Appendices A–B are retained as v2 Appendices C–D; the added material can be reliably distinguished from relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on four benchmarks, generator and probe-count ablations, and representation analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds ResNet18 evaluation, point-cloud INR classification, and regularization experiments.

M1.justification: Both versions learn per-probe latent codes through a shared deep linear generator and classify concatenated network responses with an MLP. Equations 1–2, activation removal, and data-specific generator structure are retained. The additional benchmarks do not establish a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates MNIST/FMNIST INRs and two CIFAR10 model zoos. v2 retains these and adds generalization-error prediction for ResNet18 models trained on Tiny-ImageNet subsets, plus ShapeNet point-cloud INR classification through Neural-Field-Arena. This substantially extends the evaluated data and modality coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds DWS on MNIST/FMNIST and NFN_HNP and ScaleGMN_B on MNIST/FMNIST/CIFAR10-GS. Table 2 additionally evaluates in-distribution CIFAR10 image probes. The original StatNN, Neural Graphs, and vanilla-probing comparisons remain, substantially broadening the comparison set.

E3.justification: New protocols include a zoo of over 6,000 ResNet18 models trained using ten predefined Tiny-ImageNet subsets, evaluated with 128 probes and 100-epoch probing training. v2 also introduces a point-cloud probe-budget sweep reaching 2,048 probes, a weight-decay sweep from 10^-2 to 10^-8, and in-distribution probe controls. Existing metrics and benchmark training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained linearity, depth, convolutional-structure, and interpretability analyses, v2 tests whether weight decay can substitute for linear generators (Appendix A, Table 7), examines point-cloud probe efficiency (Figure 8), and adds in-distribution controls (Table 2). These address substantial additional questions about regularization and probe selection.

E5.justification: Matched tables retain five-seed averaging and their existing uncertainty entries; Figures 4–5 retain five-seed averages. No changed run counts, uncertainty estimator, confidence intervals, or statistical tests are specified. New Tables 5, 7, and 8 report point estimates with repetitions and uncertainty unspecified.

E6.justification: Original numerical results are retained, while v2 adds baseline, control, and regularization results. New ResNet18 Kendall’s tau values are 0.910 for ProbeGen, 0.856 for StatNN, and 0.843 for vanilla probing. Point-cloud accuracy is 0.930 for ProbeGen versus 0.913 for vanilla probing with 128 probes. Figure 8 additionally reports that 32 ProbeGen probes outperform 2,048 vanilla probes.

T1.justification: The weight-classification definition, Equations 1–2, and mathematical basis for the generator remain unchanged. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or derivation appears. Added Kendall’s tau explanations describe the already-used metric.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: vanilla probing is competitive, existing learned probes are suboptimal, and deep linear generation improves generalization with substantially fewer FLOPs. Additional experiments strengthen the evidence without redefining these headline contributions.

C2.justification: Section 6 replaces an entirely prospective discussion of other modalities with preliminary point-cloud support. Appendix A newly interprets weight-decay tuning as task-dependent and deep linear generation as stable regularization. The existing output-space, weight-generation, and scalability limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The implementation appendix adds a six-layer transposed-convolution generator and 100-epoch training specification for the ResNet18 experiment. It newly states that baselines use their default hyperparameters, without establishing a change to earlier runs. Existing implementation settings and project-page access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands coverage of weight augmentation, network alignment, aligned weight spaces, and equivariant architectures. It also adds a dedicated INR discussion covering images, 3D representations, video, and audio, with corresponding references. This broadens research positioning beyond the separate citation-style conversion.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order are largely preserved. v2 adds localized INR and metric explanations, revises experimental and discussion passages, introduces related-work subheadings and social-impact/acknowledgment sections, and relabels the appendices. Publication headers, contact text, and citation style also change.

P2.justification: v2 adds three tables and a point-cloud scaling figure, expands Tables 2–3, and places the FLOPs and ResNet18 tables side by side. The ICLR layout also redistributes existing displays, particularly the appendix figures. Original figure images are retained; v1 Table 5 becomes Table 6 and Figures 8–10 become Figures 9–11.

improvement.justification: v1 supports its claims mainly through small image-model benchmarks and a limited comparison set. v2 substantially strengthens external validity through ResNet18 and point-cloud evaluations, expands relevant baselines, and tests whether ordinary weight decay explains the generator’s advantage. These additions address important gaps in scalability and regularization evidence. Missing uncertainty and detailed split documentation for the new experiments temper, but do not outweigh, these substantial gains.
